identification.summary: Silent Librarian is the name used by Proofpoint (TA407) and others, and COBALT DICKENS by Secureworks, for an Iran-linked group that runs credential-phishing campaigns against universities using fake library and student-portal login pages [S3][S5][S6]. Press reporting on Proofpoint's profile ties the names Silent Librarian, Cobalt Dickens, TA407 and Mabna Institute together [S9]. The US indictment of nine people said to work for the Mabna Institute was unsealed in March 2018 [S1][S2]. Secureworks counted at least 380 universities in over 30 countries targeted as of September 2019 [S3].
identification.firstObserved: The Mabna Institute indictment, as reported, covers intrusions against universities beginning in 2013 [S8]. Records on the 2018 indictment describe the campaign as already large by March 2018 [S1][S2].
identification.notes: Names are not perfectly interchangeable. The record's alias list pairs the Mabna Institute (the indicted company) with the Silent Librarian phishing activity; vendors such as Secureworks assess these as the same actor but that is a vendor judgment [S3]. RiskIQ observed a separate 2020 set of university phishing campaigns with similar tradecraft (domain shadowing) and named it Shadow Academy without attributing it to Mabna [S6]. Victim counts differ by source (176 vs 178 foreign universities; 320+ vs 380) [S1][S2][S3][S8].

attribution.sponsor: Iran. The 2018 US Treasury action stated the Mabna Institute acted for the benefit of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) [S2]; the indictment is reported to say the firm also served other Iranian government clients [S1].
attribution.confidence: Treasury and DOJ made the Mabna-IRGC statements in 2018 (as reported) [S1][S2]. Secureworks assessed COBALT DICKENS as an actor bound to the Iranian government [S3]. Whether every later university phishing wave is Mabna activity is a vendor linkage, not a government finding; RiskIQ declined to link its 2020 Shadow Academy cluster to Mabna [S6].
attribution.basis: US DOJ indictment and OFAC designation of Mabna Institute and individuals, March 2018 (via press and Iran Watch coverage) [S1][S2]; superseding indictment of 17 defendants unsealed August 2026 (via press coverage) [S7][S8]; vendor reporting from Secureworks, Malwarebytes and Proofpoint (via press) [S3][S5][S9].

objectives: Per the indictment as reported, the group stole academic data and intellectual property (more than 31 TB) from universities, companies and agencies, and sold the stolen articles through Iranian sites Megapaper.ir and Gigapaper.ir [S1][S8]. Treasury stated the Mabna Institute acted for the IRGC's benefit [S2].

sectors: Private-sector companies (at least 42 US and 11 foreign per the 2026 indictment)
regions: Foreign universities: 176 in 21 countries per Treasury; 178 per 2026 indictment [S2][S8]
Australia, United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Hong Kong and Switzerland in the July-August 2019 wave [S4]
targeting.notes: The 2018 indictment reportedly cites about 100,000 professor accounts targeted and 7,998 compromised [S1]. Secureworks counted at least 380 universities in over 30 countries by September 2019, many targeted repeatedly [S3]. Alleged victims also included the Labor Department, the UN and FERC [S1]. Proofpoint reports campaigns cluster around the back-to-school period, usually June to October [S9].

capabilities.summary: Low-volume, well-crafted spearphishing built on spoofed university branding and library or student-portal login pages [S9]. In 2019 Secureworks saw over 20 new Freenom domains and valid Let's Encrypt certificates on spoofed login pages, with lures sent from compromised university accounts [S3][S4]. In fall 2020 Malwarebytes saw mimic domains mainly on .ME, .TK and .CF, with lures updated for virtual classes [S5]. The 2018 indictment says compromised accounts were used to harvest research and email [S1]. No custom malware is described in the cited sources [S1][S3].

campaigns.name: Mabna Institute university intrusions
campaigns.summary: Indictment as reported alleges a campaign against 144 US and 176 foreign universities, 31+ TB stolen, with data resold in Iran [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: US indictment and OFAC sanctions
campaigns.summary: Nine Iranians indicted in SDNY and Mabna Institute plus individuals designated under E.O. 13694 on 23 March 2018 [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: Summer-fall 2019 library-themed wave
campaigns.summary: Secureworks observed over 60 universities in six countries targeted via 20+ new Freenom domains and Let's Encrypt certificates, and reported the group had not changed operations despite the indictment [S3][S4].

campaigns.name: Fall 2020 campaign
campaigns.summary: Malwarebytes learned in mid-September 2020 of a new Silent Librarian campaign using .ME, .TK and .CF domains and virtual-class lures [S5].

campaigns.name: Shadow Academy cluster (not attributed to Mabna)
campaigns.summary: RiskIQ tracked July to October 2020 phishing against 20 targets in four countries using domain shadowing; it found TTPs consistent with Silent Librarian but insufficient for attribution [S6].

campaigns.name: Superseding indictment of 17
campaigns.summary: 14-count SDNY superseding indictment unsealed 18 August 2026 adding eight defendants; reported State Department reward up to $10 million [S7][S8].

diamond.adversary: Mabna Institute staff and contractors, 17 charged individuals, working for IRGC benefit per US government statements [S2][S7][S8].
diamond.capability: Spearphishing with cloned university login pages, compromised-account lure delivery, credential theft [S3][S4][S9].
diamond.infrastructure: Freenom and later .ME/.TK/.CF domains, Let's Encrypt certificates, compromised university accounts and URL shorteners; resale sites Megapaper.ir and Gigapaper.ir [S1][S3][S5][S9].
diamond.victim: Universities worldwide, plus companies, agencies and NGOs [S2][S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Theft of academic work for IRGC benefit and for resale in Iran [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Single-factor web authentication on university library and student portals, and weak controls over lookalike domains [S3][S9].

gaps: Primary DOJ, Treasury and Proofpoint documents were not opened; DOJ and Treasury content is taken from press and Iran Watch coverage and the Proofpoint profile only from search summaries [S1][S2][S9].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: higher-education networks and research partners (including DoD-funded labs) are the observed target set [S2][S8]. Step 3: the adversary uses low-volume credential phishing with lookalike domains and compromised-account lures, timed to the academic calendar [S4][S9]. Step 4 MLCOA: renewed June-October wave against university library and student portals, harvesting credentials for research and email access [S1][S9]. MDCOA: stolen faculty or partner credentials used to pivot into defense-related research or partner mail [S1]. Candidate indicators: newly registered lookalike university domains on free TLDs, new Let's Encrypt certificates for them, and lures sent from other universities' accounts [S3][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: share university-themed phishing indicators with affiliated academic and DIB research partners via existing ISAC/DC3 channels [S2][S8]. Authorities: monitoring of non-DoD university networks rests with those owners and with law enforcement; confirm authorities before any action. Mission assurance: enforce MFA on any DoD-affiliated academic accounts and monitor for email-forwarding abuse [S1]. Coordination: align with FBI and partner universities, noting the 2026 indictment may prompt retaliation or shifts in tradecraft (unverified).

provenance.importedSummary: Last Friday, Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein announced the indictment of nine Iranians who worked for an organization named the Mabna Institute. According to prosecutors, the defendants stole more than 31 terabytes of data from universities, companies, and government agencies around the world. The cost to the universities alone reportedly amounted to approximately $3.4 billion. The information stolen from these universities was used by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) or sold for profit inside Iran. PhishLabs has been tracking this same threat group since late-2017, designating them Silent Librarian. Since discovery, we have been working with the FBI, ISAC partners, and other international law enforcement agencies to help understand and mitigate these attacks.
